title: Inequivalent modular tensor categories with identical $S$, $T$ and $W$
abstract: It remains an open question whether the modular data $(S,T)$ together with the Whitehead-link matrix $W$ determine a modular tensor category up to ribbon equivalence. We answer negatively by constructing two braided-inequivalent Dijkgraaf--Witten modular categories for $(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^3$ for prime $p\ge5$ with identical $(S,T,W)$ and, more generally, identical Reshetikhin--Turaev invariants of all framed oriented links with at most two components under a single bijection of simple objects. The construction varies an alternating $3$-cocycle while fixing a quadratic cohomology class, using restriction to subgroups of rank at most two to match link invariants and the quadratic and alternating classes together to obstruct braided equivalence. A complete classification of modular tensor categories up to ribbon equivalence therefore requires invariants beyond those of colored framed links with at most two components. We also analytically evaluate an uncolored partition function on a closed oriented three-manifold that separates all $(p-1)/2$ equivalence classes in the family.
summary: This theoretical paper proves that the modular data $(S, T, W)$ is not a complete set of invariants for classifying Modular Tensor Categories. The authors construct a family of inequivalent categories and use the partition function on a closed 3-manifold to distinguish them, showing that higher-order topological invariants are necessary for a full classification.
main_problem: The paper addresses the open question of whether the modular data $(S, T)$ together with the Whitehead-link matrix $W$ uniquely determine a Modular Tensor Category (MTC) up to ribbon equivalence.
main_result: The authors prove negatively that $(S, T, W)$ are insufficient to determine an MTC, constructing a family of braided-inequivalent categories with identical invariants.
method: They use link invariants (Reshetikhin-Turaev type) and, crucially, the uncolored partition function on a closed oriented three-manifold to distinguish between categories that share the same low-order invariants.
model_or_system: The model involves Dijkgraaf-Witten modular categories associated with the group $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^3$, whose structure is analyzed using 3-cocycles and cohomology classes.
key_observables: The uncolored partition function $Z_u(M_p)$ on a 3-manifold $M_p$ derived from a specific link surgery.
important_parameters: Prime $p \ge 5$, the structure of the group $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^3$, and the cocycle parameters $u$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes specific normalizations for link invariants and relies on the existence of a single vacuum-preserving bijection to equate the low-order invariants.
figures_summary: The notes do not describe specific figures, but the structure implies comparisons between invariants derived from different link components (1-component vs 2-component) and the final 3-component manifold invariant.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first showing agreement of link invariants for 1- and 2-component links (Section 4), then establishing algebraic constraints on equivalence (Section 5), and finally using the 3-manifold partition function (Section 7) to provide the definitive obstruction.
why_interesting: While highly abstract, the techniques of using topological invariants (like 3-manifold partition functions) to distinguish between mathematically equivalent but physically distinct quantum field theories (MTCs) are relevant to understanding the robustness of quantum information encoded in topological states.
